command: python3 scripts/verify_staged.py start; repeated next --count 5; then finish. Exact invocations and compiler argv are in process_record.json and RESULTS.json.
mathematical_claim: For every membership structure M satisfying the explicit coded ZFC theory, the internally quantified fine complete-ultrafilter principle implies compactness and residual reflection for the independently coded fixed-domain small-scope constraint class. All products, function spaces, local assignment selectors, coordinate graphs, small fiber families, intersections and final assignments are internal sets derived using actual finite-parameter Separation, Replacement and Choice axioms. A closed membership-language sentence expressing this implication is proved true in every such M.
input_domain: Arbitrary membership structures satisfying encoded ZFC; internal set-coded injection witnesses, function graphs, relation tables, scopes, ultrafilters and completeness. No external-cardinality or powerset correctness assumption.
tested_surrogate: Fresh proof elaboration, exhaustive named theorem axiom audit, predecessor source equality, expected rejection controls. Mathematical universal conclusions derive from the proof terms, not from finite enumeration.

bounds.build_strategy: Clean serial targets in hash-pinned resumable batches

pass_means: Every compilation succeeds, every named theorem is audited, axiom dependencies satisfy the standard allowlist, input hashes are unchanged, predecessor theorem sources match, and false proof and placeholder controls are rejected for the expected reasons.
failure_means: No final PASS or claim that all proofs checked. Compiler, audit, integrity or resource failures must be reported separately.
non_claims: No uncountable compactness cardinal, internal fine ultrafilter, truth of Theta or KZFC model is proved to exist or introduced as an axiom.
No full internal equivalence with complete-filter extension is proved: the internal extension-to-fine and internal compactness-to-extension arrows remain open.
The checked closed-sentence implication is a semantic consequence for every model of the encoded ZFC theory, not an extracted derivation in a separate first-order proof calculus.
Internal functions, cardinalities, powersets and completeness are not identified with external counterparts; no external well-foundedness is assumed.
No independence, relative consistency, new consistency strength, first-formalization or novelty claim.
